From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: request — vulnerability management evidence (draft attestation + artifacts)

Laura — draft attached and supporting artifacts included. Summary below and quick notes on provenance.

Summary (for SIG packet):
- Scan cadence: authenticated internal host scans (weekly), external network scans (biweekly), SCA (dependency) scanning nightly for our build pipelines. We retain scan results for 12 months. See attached vm-scan-schedule-202611.csv for examples from Oct/Nov.
- SLA commitments: critical CVEs: remediation (patch or validated mitigation) within 7 calendar days; high: 30 calendar days; medium: 90 calendar days. P0/critical emergency exceptions routed to on-call + dedicated patch window.
- Definition: 
  - "Remediation" = deploy vendor patch or rebuild with updated component such that vulnerability no longer reproduces in our testing.
  - "Mitigation" = documented compensating control (WAF rule, feature flag rollback, network ACL) that reduces exploitability while patch is scheduled. Mitigation must include expiration and action owner.
- Escalation & evidence: all remediation tickets created in Jira (VM-####) with link and closure proof (scan before/after). SOC2 auditors reviewed a sample of closures in last audit.

Attachments included: vm-scan-schedule-202611.csv (sample cadence dates), cve-closure-playbook-2026.pdf (playbook + evidence checklist).

Draft attestation text (please edit):
"On behalf of Redwood Inference, I attest that Redwood operates a documented vulnerability management program that includes weekly authenticated internal scans, biweekly external network scans, and nightly dependency scanning. Redwood commits to remediation or validated mitigation of Critical vulnerabilities within seven (7) calendar days, High within thirty (30) calendar days, and Medium within ninety (90) calendar days. Exceptions are tracked with compensating controls and documented escalation. Evidence of scan results and remediation tickets are maintained and available upon audit request."

Kimberly
Director, Information Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: vm-scan-schedule-202611.csv (CSV), cve-closure-playbook-2026.pdf (PDF)

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG: request — VM attestation draft and operational caveats

Thanks Kim — a couple of operational clarifications and the step-down language for the attestation packet.

Operational clarifications:
- Our 7-day target for Critical assumes no required code rollback across multiple services. For multi-service coordinated changes we escalate to a hot-patch workflow and notify affected customers. We track Mean Time To Remediate (MTTR) per severity and will include a small sample of MTTRs for the last six months if SIG requests metrics.
- For immediate compensating controls we can add temporary firewall rules, rate-limiting via edge, and targeted feature toggles. Those are logged and have owners with expiration dates.

Suggested step-down paragraph (to include below attestation):
"If a vendor patch cannot be applied immediately, Redwood implements compensating technical controls (for example, targeted WAF rules, network ACLs, or traffic shaping) and documents an owner and expiry for the compensating control. The control is validated by red-team or internal test scans and tracked in the remediation ticket until a permanent fix is deployed."

I'll provide a short CSV of MTTR samples (critical/high) by EOD Monday if they want metrics; otherwise the attestation + artifacts should satisfy intake.

Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
